sections.h2: How to Make a Product Photo in 3 Simple Steps
paras: Upload Your Product Photo. A phone picture of the tan handbag on a pale surface is enough. If you would rather not upload yet, write one sentence about that clean studio surface and soft light.

Describe Your Scene. For the handbag, ask for it alone on white when you need the first image on the product page. Ask for a hand lifting it only when you want a use shot. Describe the look in plain words.
Download and Post. When the bag looks right, download the square file. If the clasp or the metal looks wrong, write a shorter note and run it again. That still can later be the first frame of a clip.

sections.h2: Where Should Each Handbag Photo Go?
paras: A marketplace hero and a social post can come from the same handbag photo, once you pick the destination. A marketplace hero has stricter rules than a social post.

A first image usually wants a clean white field and nothing extra in the frame. Later photos can show the bag in a kraft box, in use, or as a detail. On your own store, match the backdrop you already use so the row stays tidy. A square file fits a product page and a social crop, and you can also pick 9:16, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4.

sections.h2: How Do I Check a Photo Before I Publish It?
paras: Put the image beside the tan handbag in your hand. Compare color, shape, the hardware, the strap, and how many pieces there are.

Zoom in on the handbag's label, hardware, and edges. If something is wrong, render again from a sharper photo or a clearer sentence instead of hiding it with a caption. Use your own label and your own logo. The picture should say only what is really on the bag. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded. Uploads and results stay in your account and are not shown publicly.
